text:
Every afternoon in the garden,
as evening is about to fall,
the sultan’s lovely daughter
descends to stroll there.

Beside the ringing fountain
she sometimes pauses,
watching the clear jets leap
and hearing them fall.

Every afternoon, as evening falls,
the handsome slave comes too,
and calmly he is seen
beside the fountain, listening
to the jets as well.

Each afternoon his face grows paler.
One day the princess hurries up to him:
“What is your name? What is your homeland, slave?”
“Arabia gave me birth;
they called me Mohammed.
I am of those Azraites
who die when they truly love.”

translation.title: Every Afternoon in the Garden
translation.editorial_note: Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
